title: U.S. Senate · Idaho

context.text: David Roth won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for this seat (61.9% of the vote) but is listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn or disqualified and does not appear as a candidate in the November 3 general election.
Jim Risch defeated Josh Roy, Joe Evans, and Denny LaVe in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 67.3% of the vote.

summary.text: Jim Risch is the incumbent Republican U.S. Senator from Idaho, first elected in 2008 and now serving his third term. He previously served as Idaho's Governor, Lieutenant Governor, and in the Idaho State Senate.

background.text: Received a bachelor's degree in forestry and a Juris Doctorate from the University of Idaho.
Elected to two terms as Ada County Prosecuting Attorney, then served in the Idaho State Senate, where he was elected Republican Majority Leader and President Pro Tempore.
Twice elected Idaho's Lieutenant Governor, then elected Idaho's 31st Governor in 2006.
Outside public service, has worked as a rancher, small business owner, and former senior partner of the Risch Goss Insinger Gustavel law firm.

priorities.text: Lists protecting the Second Amendment, advocating for energy independence, blocking federal overreach, and defending Idaho agriculture and natural resources among his priorities in the Senate.

positions.summary: His official Senate website lists 'protecting the Second Amendment' among the priorities that define his record in the Senate.

record.text: Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.
Serves on the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship, the Select Committee on Ethics, and the Select Committee on Intelligence.
As Governor of Idaho (2006-2007), cut property taxes by 20% and secured $100 million in additional funding for Idaho's public schools, according to his official Senate biography.

candidates.name: Matt Loesby

summary.text: Matt Loesby is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Idaho. He was born in Glenwood Springs, Colorado, earned a bachelor's degree from Chapman University in 2010, and has worked as a software engineer.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Chapman University in 2010.
Has worked as a software engineer.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, or public policy statements found beyond a brief Ballotpedia biography.

candidates.name: Todd Achilles

summary.text: Todd Achilles is an Independent candidate for U.S. Senate, an Army veteran, former Idaho state legislator, public policy professor, and business executive who resigned from the Idaho House of Representatives in July 2025 to run.

background.text: Served as a U.S. Army tank commander and armor officer.
Spent over 20 years in senior leadership roles at T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard, and several technology startups.
Served in the Idaho House of Representatives before resigning in July 2025 to launch his U.S. Senate campaign.

priorities.text: Says stopping corruption in Congress is his first priority, citing support for term limits, getting money out of elections, overturning Citizens United, banning congressional stock trading, ending the revolving door between Congress and lobbying, and stopping gerrymandering.
priorities.quote: Washington is broken because politicians answer to parties and donors instead of voters.

priorities.text: Says he would work to strengthen the middle class through measures including shrinking the national debt, breaking up monopolies, eliminating corporate and high-income tax loopholes, and raising wages by rolling back right-to-work laws.
Prioritizes protecting Idaho's public lands, including preserving access, investing in conservation and land management, and supporting rural economies tied to outdoor recreation.

positions.summary: Supports eliminating corporate and high-income tax loopholes as part of a plan to strengthen the middle class.
positions.quote: eliminating corporate and high income tax loopholes

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no independent campaign website content reviewed.

candidates.name: Natalie Fleming

summary.text: Natalie Fleming is an Independent candidate for U.S. Senate from Idaho's high desert, describing herself as a rancher's daughter and mother with a background in software, information technology, supply chain management, and cybersecurity.

background.text: Graduated from Moscow High School and returned to Idaho in 2002 as a single mother.
Earned degrees in Information Technology Management, Supply Chain Management, and Cybersecurity.
Has written two books, one on countering hate propaganda and one on restoring the water cycle.

priorities.text: Says she is running to rein in authoritarianism and mass surveillance, including opposing tracking technology and calling for limits on AI and data brokers.
priorities.quote: I'll push for real limits on AI, an end to mass surveillance in every form, and a tech industry that answers to the people it serves instead of building the infrastructure to control them.

priorities.text: Prioritizes what she calls household security: reducing housing costs driven by institutional investors buying single-family homes, and using degraded federal land for housing instead.
Supports restoring Idaho farmland and rangeland through regenerative grazing and land policy that rewards restoration over extraction.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no independent campaign website content reviewed. None of her stated priorities map cleanly onto the guide's fixed issue list, so no Position entries were added.
